headings.text: Iterating on rmapi against the cluster

blocks.html:
This page is about working on the platform from your own machine: spinning up a local cluster, editing manifests, and iterating on whatever service you're focused on.

If you haven't yet, skim Architecture first so the phases and folder layout below don't come out of nowhere.

Prerequisites

The repo pins tool versions through mise. Once mise is installed, it picks up the right kubectl, kind, helm, yq, task, and zarf when you cd into the directory.

# one-time
mise install        # installs the versions listed in mise.toml
mise trust          # trust the local mise.toml

# also needed (not managed by mise)
docker              # kind runs nodes as containers

Versions live in ../mise.toml. Without mise, install matching versions of kubectl 1.36, kind 0.31, helm 3, task 3, yq 4.53.2, and zarf 0.76.0 by hand.

Bring up a local environment

task up        # creates the kind cluster and runs all four deploy phases
task           # list every available task
task down      # tear the kind cluster down (alias for `cluster:delete`)

task up is safe to re-run. It won't recreate the cluster if opendefense-kind is already there. The cluster name and port mappings come from ../kind-config.yaml, which pre-binds ports 80 and 443 along with the TAK and MediaMTX ports to localhost.

When it's done, the UI is at https://localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi/. The hostname is just a public DNS record pointing at 127.0.0.1, so you don't have to mess with /etc/hosts.

If task deploy falls over partway through a phase, it's usually a controller from the previous phase that hasn't reported Ready yet. Re-running the same command is enough. The wait gates carry on from where they stopped.

Working in a service folder

Every service follows the same layout:

k8s/<service>/
├── base/
│   ├── kustomization.yaml
│   └── resources/...              # Deployment, Service, PVC, namespace, ...
└── overlays/
    ├── local/
    │   └── kustomization.yaml   # hostnames, image overrides, env patches
    └── cloud/
        └── kustomization.yaml

Examples worth copying from:

  • k8s/battlelog/base/kustomization.yaml, a simple app with a database.
  • k8s/pvarki-pki/base/kustomization.yaml, CA and cert plumbing.
  • k8s/traefik/base/kustomization.yaml, a Helm-chart-backed base.

Rules of thumb:

  • Keep base/ environment-agnostic: no hostnames, no environment registries, no env-specific certificates, placeholder images only.
  • Anything environment-specific (image tags, ingress routes, certificates, env patches) belongs in the overlays, and each environment gets its own overlays/<env>/kustomization.yaml.
  • Try to keep one concern per change. A routing tweak, an image bump, and a cert change are three separate commits, not one.
  • Helm-backed bases need --enable-helm. traefik, trust-manager, external-secrets-operator, and a few others render Helm charts inside Kustomize. Build and apply them with --enable-helm.

After editing, render the overlay locally before you apply:

kubectl kustomize --enable-helm k8s/battlelog/overlays/local
kubectl kustomize --enable-helm k8s/main/local/opendefense

If you change the composition (a service moves to a different phase, or a new one shows up) keep ../taskfile.yaml in sync, since that's what owns the rollout wait gates between phases.

Iterating on rmapi against the cluster

mirrord lets you run rmapi locally while that local process still sees the cluster's traffic, secrets, and filesystem. The flow is roughly:

  1. task up so opendefense-rmapi is live in the opendefense-system namespace.

  2. In the python-rasenmaeher-api checkout, run:

    mirrord exec --steal \
  --target-namespace opendefense-system \
  --target deployment/opendefense-rmapi -- \
  bash -c 'JWT_PRIVKEY_PATH=./locadir/private/rm_jwtsign.key \
           JWT_PUBKEY_PATH=./locadir/public \
           poetry run uvicorn --reload --factory \
             rasenmaeher_api.web.application:get_app'

    --steal redirects in-cluster traffic to your local process instead of the deployed pod. Reloads hit your code immediately.

Common local workflows

Task Command
List available tasks task
Bring everything up from scratch task up
Re-apply after editing manifests task deploy
Render a single overlay to YAML kubectl kustomize --enable-helm k8s/<svc>/overlays/local
Watch a rollout kubectl -n opendefense-system get pods -w
Tear the cluster down task down
Check current kube context kubectl config current-context

When something goes wrong

  • If task deploy hangs on a rollout wait, look at the deployment and its pods with kubectl describe deployment <name> -n <ns>. The wait gates in taskfile.yaml tell you which deployments it's blocking on.
  • error: unable to recognize "...": no matches for kind after an edit means a CRD from infra-phase1 isn't there yet. Run task deploy and let phase 1 settle before you re-apply.
  • Forbidden errors during apply are usually a server-side-apply field ownership conflict, typically on something Helm or a human created earlier. Dig into it before forcing anything. Don't just slap --force-conflicts on everything.
  • TLS errors between pods usually mean the consumer namespace never got its CA bundle from trust-manager. Those bundles are namespace-scoped and only show up once infra-phase2 is healthy.
